results.content: # Critical JFrog Artifactory Vulnerability Reportedly Exploited in the Wild. Exploitation of the authentication bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-82329 started just days after its public disclosure. **A critical vulnerability in JFrog Artifactory is reportedly being exploited in the wild just days after its public disclosure.**. Artifactory updates released on August 28 patch CVE-2026-82329, a critical authentication bypass vulnerability that can lead to admin access. Exposure management firm WatchTowr reported on Tuesday that it has already seen in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-82329, “with attackers minting themselves admin tokens”. *SecurityWeek* has reached out to JFrog for confirmation of in-the-wild exploitation and will update this article if the company responds. CVE-2026-82329 may be the first Artifactory vulnerability exploited in malicious attacks, but it’s not the first to be exploited. results.title: Critical JFrog Artifactory Vulnerability Reportedly Exploited in the Wild - SecurityWeek

results.content: # ServiceNow Patches 3 Critical Code Injection Vulnerabilities. Attackers could exploit the security defects to execute arbitrary code and access or tamper with data. **ServiceNow has announced patches for four vulnerabilities, including three critical code injection flaws in the ServiceNow AI platform, each with a maximum severity (CVSS score of 10/10).**. The first of the critical bugs, tracked as CVE-2026-18885, allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code in the ServiceNow platform under certain circumstances. An attacker could exploit the weakness to gain access to and potentially modify arbitrary data, ServiceNow notes in its advisory. Tracked as CVE-2026-74820, the third critical vulnerability is an SQL injection flaw that allows an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL statements against the underlying ServiceNow database. An attacker could exploit the bug to “gain access to, or modify, instance data beyond what was intended,” ServiceNow says. An attacker could exploit the security defect to gain “more access to the Now Platform than intended,” the company says.
results.title: ServiceNow Patches 3 Critical Code Injection Vulnerabilities - securityweek.com

results.content: # Nightmare Eclipse Drops ‘HardBreacher’ Kaspersky Product Exploit. Kaspersky told SecurityWeek that it patched the vulnerability affecting its Endpoint Security product. **The researcher known as Nightmare Eclipse has dropped another zero-day — this time a privilege escalation exploit targeting a Kaspersky endpoint security product.**. Nightmare Eclipse, also known as Chaotic Eclipse, has released PoC exploits for many vulnerabilities in recent months, mainly Windows and Microsoft Defender flaws. Over the weekend, Nightmare Eclipse released an exploit targeting a privilege escalation vulnerability in Kaspersky Endpoint Security. **Related**: Critical Ruby on Rails Vulnerability in Attackers’ Crosshairs. **Related**: More Details Emerge on Exploited PaperCut Vulnerabilities. In this article:Chaotic Eclipse, HardBreacher, Kaspersky, PoC exploit, security products, vulnerability, Zero-Day.
